transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Time: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~42m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Arjun Patel (Redwood SE), Samira Lopez (Redwood Solutions), Laura Kim (Ponterra Head of ML), Diego Ramos (Platform), Nora Patel (CTO), Alexis Ford (SRE)

Summary: quick sync on KV hit-rate after last week's prefetch change, discuss prompt reuse patterns, eviction TTL adjustments, and next perf run. Some transcription glitches (names, acronyms).

Topics: prefetch tuning, prefix matching, KV cache hit-rate trends, prompt dedup/reuse, eviction policy (TTL vs LRU), security notes (K-M-S, SOC two), next perf run scheduling

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining — can you see my screen?
[00:07] Laura: yep, we're good. thanks Maya.
[00:10] Maya: cool. quick agenda: review the hit-rate delta since we flipped prefetch window, talk through a couple of outliers Diego flagged, then propose a small TTL tweak and plan the 2x perf run.
[00:22] Diego: yeah i pulled the logs, there's an immediate bump in prefix hits, like +9 percent first 24 hours, but then we see a sag at certain times of day, uh around 2am pst where hit-rate drops.
[00:34] Arjun: hmmm, is that correlated with session affinity expiration or eviction? are you seeing evictions at that window?
[00:39] Diego: some evictions, yes — our metric shows short bursts of free-up when batch jobs run, so looks like a TTL collision with nightly batch.
[00:47] Maya: okay that's useful. when we talked last week we suggested a staggered TTL and sliding prefetch of 6-8 tokens for the long tail; we provided a JSON blob — did you pick up that config?
[00:58] Laura: we pulled the blob, but we tweaked it to a 4-token prefetch to avoid overshooting. wife — i mean, we wanted to be conservative. (laughs)
[01:10] Samira: (overlap) we also suggested switching prefix-match mode from strict to fuzzy for prompts that have variable user identifiers, so you don't miss hits due to small user id drift.
[01:18] Alexis: quick q — fuzzy matching increases false positives? could that return stale context?
[01:23] Arjun: good question — fuzzy in our case is configurable threshold on normalized prompt distance, not a pure fuzzy string match. it's designed to prefer earlier tokens and require strong prefix overlap for KV keys; false positives are rare if you keep threshold high.
[01:36] Nora: do we have an example where fuzzy caused incorrect completions? i'm worried about hallucination risk.
[01:42] Arjun: we saw one in POC two where a similar legal clause from another account was pulled; that's why we recommend account-scoped prefixes and a conservative threshold. also, fallbacks to model variant are quick if prefix confidence is low.
[01:55] Diego: log note: we have multi-tenant keys, so scoping is important — we did an interim with tenant-prefixing but we may need to salt the key with session hash too.
[02:05] Maya: ok, action item — we'll add salted session id example to the runbook.
[02:09] Laura: thanks. on hit-rate, the dashboard shows a persistent low in the 02:00–03:00 window across three days. could be a cron job — Diego to confirm?
[02:20] Diego: yep i'll correlate. also noticed that when the nightly ETL locks the DB, some of our feature lookup timeouts cause clients to refresh sessions which busts prefix reuse.
[02:33] Maya: hmm that explains the burst of new keys. two-pronged approach: (1) increase session TTL around that window, (2) prefetch more aggressively right before the ETL window.
[02:44] Laura: what's the cost delta you expect with prefetch bump?
[02:47] Arjun: rough ballpark — prefetch +2 tokens on 20% of traffic gives ~3–5% token cost increase, but hit-rate improvement can reduce overall calls by similar percentage — net neutral sometimes net-positive. exact depends on sequence length.
[03:00] Alexis: question on metrics— do we have token-level attribution by route? can we filter to only the inference route?
[03:06] Samira: yes the console has per-route token breakdown; we'll share a link to the filter (link: https://redwood.app/console/ponterra/metrics).
[03:14] Nora: legal/security — quick Q: you mentioned K-M-S integration; we need short note to legal about key rotation and where logs live.
[03:21] Samira: yes we'll send an HSM/KMS one-pager and SOC2 summary (note: sock two). it's in the security folder, i'll attach.
[03:29] Laura: perfect. back to tuning — Diego you mentioned spikes of new kv keys from retries; are clients deduping prompts?
[03:36] Diego: not consistently. we saw some duplication from mobile retries; we can add idempotent request ids but it's work.
[03:43] Arjun: we also recommend client-side prompt normalization: strip timestamps, stable order, canonicalize whitespace — that alone gave one customer +12% reuse.
[03:53] Laura: can you share the normalization script?
[03:55] Maya: yes, will include in the runbook link.
[03:58] Diego: small nit — the console auto-sample shows 'prefix reuse' metric but it's sometimes hard to map to actual completions. can you add a trace id for matching?
[04:06] Arjun: we can add a correlation id export; that would let you join the sample to your logs.
[04:11] Diego: perfect.
[04:14] Maya: demo quick look — (shares screen) this is the new hit-rate by hour chart, see the night dip? here's the prefetch window change we pushed: prefetch=4 -> 6 in staging then to 4 in prod like Laura said.
[04:26] Laura: so that shift is why the first-day bump then drop — we under-estimated eviction pressure.
[04:32] Arjun: i'd propose two small tests: A) keep prefetch=6 but increase KV TTL by 30% during 00:00–04:00 window; B) keep TTL and add small staggered TTL per session hash. test A is simpler.
[04:44] Nora: timeline for tests? we need results before next exec review 3/12.
[04:49] Maya: we can get 48-hr results if we start tonight, Arjun can run the load test on weekend with Alexis.
[04:57] Alexis: i'll schedule the synthetic run and set traffic profile to mimic 9am peak and night low.
[05:03] Diego: note — we may need to throttle prefetch at very high concurrency; otherwise GPU utilization spikes and costs blow up.
[05:12] Arjun: yep we have adaptive prefetch that scales down at high QPS; we'll tune threshold.
[05:17] Laura: curious — how does this play with dedicated vs hosted — are we seeing different eviction patterns on your dedicated pools?
[05:24] Maya: in Dedicated you get more predictable memory and longer-lived caches because pools are isolated; hosted pools share memory and so eviction can be noisier. that's why we often advise Reserved capacity for high reuse workloads.
[05:36] Nora: price delta? we've got finance breathing down.
[05:39] Maya: rough numbers: Dedicated adds a fixed monthly reservation but reduces per-token variable cost ~10–20% for heavy sustained usage. we'll send the pricing slice.
[05:48] Laura: okay thanks.
[05:50] Diego: small FYI — there's an odd pattern where some very short prompts never hit because prefix is normalized to long canonical form, maybe due to pre-tokenization mismatch between client and runtime.
[06:01] Arjun: that's a classic— we should sync tokenization. do you use a custom tokenizer or standard byte-level BPE?
[06:08] Diego: we use internal normalized whitespace but otherwise standard; still, small diffs.
[06:12] Arjun: i'll share a quick tokenizer check script.
[06:15] Laura: cool.
[06:17] Maya: okay to recap next steps — share runbook + pref config, Diego to run 48-hr baseline with adjusted TTL, Arjun+Alexis to schedule perf run, Samira send SOC2/KMS notes. anything else?
[06:29] Nora: add legal points: data residency note for EU customers in config.
[06:33] Samira: noted.
[06:35] Laura: also, could we get an alert when hit-rate drops >5% vs rolling mean?
[06:40] Arjun: yes alerting rule is easy; we'll add to the dashboard and share link.
[06:45] Maya: great. thanks everyone. we'll follow up in the ticket and send configs.
[06:50] (meeting closes, small crosstalk)
